items.title: Senior Advocate TR Rajagopalan passes away
items.summary: Senior Advocate TR Rajagopalan , a senior member of the Madras Bar Association and former Additional Advocate General of Tamil Nadu, passed away on Saturday, November 14. Rajagopalan practised before the Madras High Court, appearing in civil disputes, writ proceedings and matters concerning education, government policy and environmental regulation. As Additional Advocate General, he represented the Tamil Nadu government in several proceedings. These included a batch of petitions concerning the appointment and remuneration of teachers in aided schools, decided by the High Court in 1999. Justice SS Sundar and Pushpa Satyanarayanan were among the lawyers who trained in his chambers. In 2006, Rajagopalan represented the Cricket Association of Pondicherry before the Madras High Court in proceedings concerning its application for membership of the Board of Control for Cricket in India. He also appeared for Sterlite Industries before the National Green Tribunal in 2013, challenging the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board’s direction to close its copper plant in Thoothukudi. items.title: From US midterms to AP local body polls, how data centres are becoming an election issue
items.summary: Follow TNM ’ s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Without missing a beat, Alla Saroja responded quickly to the question posed to her. “This victory is one for the farmers and one against data centres," she said. “It shouldn’t be viewed as a personal victory.” In Bhogapuram, two farmers took their fight against data centres from the streets to the ballot box and won. Alla Saroja and Godla Seshagiri, who contested independently from ward divisions one and two in the November 4 and 5 Andhra Pradesh local body elections, defeated their rivals on a plank that no political party was willing to touch. Both these farmers centred their campaigns around their opposition to data centres. Their victories come alongside the 2026 US midterm elections, in which opposition to data centre expansions were a significant electoral issue. The November 3 results in the US offered a striking example of how opposition to data centres moved beyond campaign speeches and into the ballot box.
